name: Question-answering computer
definition: A computer holding broad knowledge that answers arbitrary factual questions put to it in ordinary language.

milestones2.what: MIT's START natural-language system went online on the Internet in 1993 and answered English questions on many topics (Boris Katz, MIT)

sources.title: Boris Katz
sources.quote: Boris Katz is the creator of the START information processing system (since 1993 - on the Internet)

sources.title: Boris Katz
sources.quote: START natural language system that allows the user to access various types of information using English

milestones2.note: START (1993) answered open-ended English questions about places, people, movies and more over the Web, an earlier broad-domain system than Watson 2011; its knowledge came from hand-annotated sources so breadth is limited (hence low). BASEBALL 1961, LUNAR 1971, SHRDLU, Unix Consultant and LILOG are narrow-domain; Ask Jeeves 1996 matched questions to web pages; Wolfram Alpha 2009 and Watson 2011 are later.

name: Touchscreen and gesture interface
definition: Controlling a machine by touching a screen or panel, or by hand gestures and gloves read by sensors.

milestones2.what: E. A. Johnson (Royal Radar Establishment, Malvern) published a finger-driven capacitive touchscreen for air traffic control

sources.title: Touchscreen
sources.quote: He described his work on capacitive touchscreens in a short article published in 1965

milestones2.note: Earlier: AT&T Harmon 1962 patent for a light-beam stylus touchscreen (patent only, not shown working). Data gloves: Sayre Glove 1977, later. Light pens (1950s) are pointing devices, not touch.
milestones2.check_note: Earlier: Philco 1946 stylus patent (overlay on TV, not touch input), AT&T Harmon 1962 light-beam patent (patent only, no working system shown), Graham 1963 light-pen patent. Johnson 1965 is the first finger-driven touchscreen per Wikipedia. Gesture side: nothing earlier controlling a machine fits (theremin is a musical instrument, not machine control).

milestones2.what: PLATO IV terminals, introduced at the University of Illinois in 1972, had a built-in 16x16 infrared touch panel students used to answer questions

sources.title: PLATO (computer system)
sources.quote: In 1972, with the introduction of PLATO IV, Bitzer declared general success

sources.title: PLATO (computer system)
sources.quote: Touch panel: A 16×16 grid infrared touch panel, allowing students to answer questions by touching anywhere on the screen.

milestones2.note: CERN's touchscreen was put to use in 1973; PLATO IV touch panels were part of the 1972 classroom system (Wikipedia Touchscreen dates the optical patent filing to 1972). Johnson's ATC touchscreen and the 1970 Telefunken device were described in the 1960s-70 but no fetched source gives deployed use earlier.

milestones2.what: Touchscreen phones were rapidly gaining popularity by 2009 after the 2007 LG Prada and iPhone

sources.title: Touchscreen
sources.quote: By 2009, touchscreen-enabled phones were rapidly gaining popularity

milestones2.note: Date is a judgement (2007-2010). iPhone announced Jan 2007; first-pass 2007 date replaced by when popularity is stated.
milestones2.check_note: Earlier touchscreens in ATMs, kiosks, HP-150 (1983), IBM Simon (1993), Nintendo DS (2004) were niche or early-stage, not routine use by ordinary people; 2009 majority of smartphones shipping with touchscreens (Wikipedia) supports 2007-2009 as the mass-adoption window.

name: Robot vacuum cleaner and lawn mower
definition: A small autonomous machine that cleans floors or mows a lawn on its own.

milestones2.what: Whirlpool demonstrated a track-following robotic floor sweeper concept (Donald Moore's 1957 patent) at the American National Exhibition in Moscow

sources.title: Robotic vacuum cleaner
sources.quote: Whirlpool demonstrated the concept at the 1959 American National Exhibition but did not bring it to market.

milestones2.note: Follows a track under the floor, so only a loose fit to 'on its own'. Later: MowBot 1969, Electrolux Trilobite 1996, Roomba 2002. Heinlein 1956 was fiction.

milestones2.what: MowBot, autonomous robotic lawn mower patented by S. Lawrence Bellinger, sold for about $800

sources.title: Robotic lawn mower
sources.quote: In 1969, the MowBot was introduced and patented by S Lawrence Bellinger having many features of today's most popular products.

milestones2.note: No earlier robot mower or vacuum on sale found in the pages read. Trilobite (1996) and Roomba (2002) are later. Whether MowBot was truly autonomous rests on this one source.

name: Neural implant and cyborg augmentation
definition: An electronic device implanted in or joined to the human body or brain to restore or extend senses, memory or ability.

milestones2.what: Djourno and Eyries in France invented the original cochlear implant, stimulating the auditory nerve electrically.

sources.title: Cochlear implant
sources.quote: André Djourno and Charles Eyriès invented the original cochlear implant in 1957.

milestones2.note: Earlier than the first-pass House 1961. Cardiac pacemaker implants (1958) are body implants not neural/sensory, so rejected for this concept.

milestones2.what: Hochmair's multichannel cochlear implant was first implanted in a person in Vienna, followed by Clark's in 1978; both were commercialized.

sources.title: Cochlear implant
sources.quote: with the Hochmairs' device first implanted in a person in December 1977 and Clark's in August 1978

milestones2.note: House/3M single-channel devices were marketed from 1972 and FDA-approved for adults in 1984 (not verified with a fetched quote), which may be earlier practical use. Date here is a weak proxy.

name: Service robot for the public
definition: A robot that serves customers or the public as a waiter, bartender, clerk, receptionist or guide.
doubt: No milestone survived verification. Hospital delivery robots (late 1980s) and others exist, but no page could be fetched; 63 pairs score 0. A gap in sourcing, not in history.
search_hints: 1980s hospital delivery robots (Transitions Research Corp. HelpMate, first hospital use), other robots serving the public (restaurants, hotels, museums) before 2014.

definition: Computers that measure audiences, score customers and predict what they will buy.
doubt: Lost its milestone (the first pass had 1958 credit scoring): no page could be fetched. A gap in sourcing, not in history.
